Three Days in Tbilisi: A Practical Travel Guide

Tbilisi is the capital of Georgia and home to about 1,250,000 people. The old town sits on both banks of the Mtkvari river, and most sights are within walking distance of each other. This guide covers three days, a realistic budget and the mistakes first-time visitors make.

Day 1: The Old Town and Narikala

Start at Freedom Square and walk down to the sulfur baths in Abanotubani. A private room costs about 45 GEL per hour on weekdays. From the baths, take the cable car up to Narikala fortress: a one-way ticket costs 2.5 GEL and the ride takes three minutes.

Locals recommend visiting the baths early in the morning, before the tour groups arrive.

Day 2: Markets and Museums

The Dry Bridge market opens around 10 in the morning and is busiest at weekends. Spend the afternoon in the Georgian National Museum, where the gold collection alone is worth the 15 GEL ticket.

Day 3: A Day Trip to Mtskheta

Mtskheta is 20 kilometres north of the city. Minibuses leave from Didube station every 15 minutes and the trip takes about 30 minutes. In summer, 37% of visitors make this trip, so go early.

Practical tips

  • Carry cash: small cafes and minibuses rarely take cards.
  • Buy a Metromoney card for the metro and buses; it costs 2 GEL.
  • Learn a few words of Georgian; locals appreciate it.
